predecessors.note: The Imamate was destroyed in 1672; the Sultanate was "Preceded by: the Imamate of Aussa and the Dankali Sultanate" (infobox).

successors.note: "1 April 1936, completely occupied the sultanate"; the infobox says it was succeeded by Italian East Africa. The Sultan was restored in 1943-44 (Alimirah Hanfare from 1944) within Ethiopia.

capitals.name: Aussa (Asaita)
capitals.note: Infobox: capital at Aussa (also called Asaita); coordinates approximate.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria lacks the Sultanate). Infobox area 76,868 km2, "Today part of Ethiopia, Eritrea, and Djibouti"; the Afar admin-1 of Ethiopia is 101,413 km2 on the grid (ratio 0.76 against the infobox, within a factor of two); the Eritrean and Djibouti parts are not drawn.

ledger.note: 1734: Data Kadafo of the Mudaito clan seizes power and founds the sultanate. "In 1734, the Afar leader Data Kadafo, head of the Mudaito clan, seized power"; infobox "Established 1734". The founder is also Kedafu, Kadafo or Kandhafo; the land is my reading of the Afar lowlands.

1 April 1936: Italy occupies the sultanate. "1 April 1936, completely occupied the sultanate" (Aussa had signed a protectorate treaty with the Italians on 6 December 1889). The infobox: disestablished 1936.
April 1936: the sultanate ends in Italian East Africa; Ethiopia's restored government captured Sultan Muhammad Yayyo in 1943 and replaced him with Alimirah Hanfare (the Sultan's ascension in 1944).

wars.name: Aussa-Egyptian war (Munzinger)
wars.outcome: "Sultan Mahammad ibn Hanfadhe defeated and killed Werner Munzinger in 1875," who was leading an Egyptian army.

wars.name: Battle of Arraddo
wars.outcome: Welde Giyorgis Aboye "defeated Sultan Muhammad Hanfare at the battle of Arraddó in January 1896"; the page does not say what land changed hands.
wars.note: Aussa had been an Italian protectorate since 6 December 1889.

wars.name: Italian occupation of Aussa
wars.outcome: Italian forces "completely occupied the sultanate" on 1 April 1936.

certainty.note: Afar lowlands without a fixed boundary.

sources.title: Sultanate of Aussa
sources.note: Imamate of Aussa 1577-1672, Harar breaks away 1647, Mudaito sultanate from 1734, Munzinger 1875, Italian protectorate 6 Dec 1889, Arraddo Jan 1896, Italian occupation 1 April 1936. Infobox area 76,868 km2.

notes:
New dossier: Cliopatria lacks Aussa. One page opened (Sultanate of Aussa; budget 1-2). Not settled: the Italian protectorate (6 December 1889) as a vassal relation, which the Italian dossier (af-08 italian-africa) could record as vassal_start/vassal_end for 'sultanate-of-aussa'; the 1834 Battle of Darma (the page names no opponent); the extent into Eritrea and Djibouti; rulers (the page's list is incomplete: Kedafu 1734-1749, Mahammad Yayyo 1927-1936 in the infobox or 1927-1944 in the list). After 1943-44 the Sultan lived within Ethiopia (Alimirah Hanfare 1944-1975 and 1991-2011), a vassal-like relation the page leaves undated. Area: infobox 76,868 km2 against 101,413 km2 on the grid for the Afar admin-1 (0.76).
Gazetteer: all names resolved except Aussa/Asaita (approximate capital coordinate).
